scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by telling the intern to throw her banana peel in the trash. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, the setting: I work in a building where you have to walk from the parking lot down a 100-foot-long sidewalk to get to the entrance. On one side of this sidewalk, there are low-growing evergreen shrubs, and on the other side, there are trash cans at both ends. Recently, there have been a lot of flies buzzing around the area, so much so that the building manager had to call an exterminator. This morning, I saw an intern from one of the companies in the building walking in while eating a banana. She was about three-quarters of the way down the sidewalk when she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. At that point, the nearest trash can was only about 25 feet away. I was a bit upset because I wasn't caffeinated enough to be polite, so I blurted out, "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" with a hand gesture. The intern got defensive, claiming that the banana peel is organic and feeds the animals. She was half-yelling and half-crying. I pointed out the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to pick it up. Instead, she cried loudly, got the peel, and threw it in the trash. I thought that was the end of it, hoping she wouldn't litter again and that we'd have fewer flies. Later, her boss approached me and asked if I had confronted her intern. I explained the situation, and I think she spent the whole morning crying about how mean I was and couldn't do any work. My initial thought was that she was being dramatic, but I apologized for upsetting her. We both laughed about how absurd the situation was, especially over a banana peel. Now, on the weekend, I'm wondering if I overreacted. Was it appropriate for me to call her out like that? Okay, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things: 1. **The Impact of Littering**: Throwing banana peels into bushes might seem harmless, but it can attract flies and other pests, which was already a problem in the area. So, from a practical standpoint, it's better to dispose of waste properly to maintain cleanliness and hygiene. 2. **Workplace Etiquette**: As an employee, especially someone in a supervisory role, it's important to set a good example and encourage others to follow workplace rules. However, the way I confronted her was abrupt and not very kind, which might have contributed to her emotional reaction. 3. **Communication Style**: I was not at my best because I wasn't caffeinated, which led me to react impulsively. A more calm and respectful approach might have been more effective in getting the desired outcome without causing distress. 4. **Consequences of My Action**: The intern ended up crying and complaining to her boss, which led to an uncomfortable situation for both of us. While I apologized, it's clear that my approach had unintended negative consequences. 5. **Alternative Approaches**: Maybe I could have addressed the issue more gently, perhaps by asking her to dispose of the peel properly rather than confronting her in an aggressive manner. 6. **Personal Feelings vs. Professional Responsibilities**: It's important to balance personal feelings with professional duties. While I felt it was important to address the littering, the way I did it might have been counterproductive. 7. **Learning Opportunity**: This situation could serve as a learning experience for both of us. For me, it's a reminder to approach such situations with more patience and tact. For the intern, it's an opportunity to understand the importance of proper waste disposal and workplace etiquette. 8. **Workplace Culture**: The reaction of the intern and her boss might reflect the overall workplace culture. If employees feel that they can't handle minor conflicts without escalating them, it might indicate a need for better conflict resolution training or a more supportive environment. 9. **My Role in the Conflict**: I need to take responsibility for my part in the conflict. While I had valid concerns about littering, my approach was confrontational and not conducive to a positive resolution. 10. **Moving Forward**: It's important to move past this incident and ensure that it doesn't affect our working relationship negatively. I should focus on maintaining a respectful and professional demeanor in the future. In summary, while my intention was to address a practical issue related to cleanliness and pest control, my approach was inappropriate and led to unnecessary emotional distress for the intern. It would have been better to handle the situation with more kindness and professionalism, ensuring that the message was conveyed without causing offense or upset.
